description:
FILED s523b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-20) from #3529's measurement.  A STASH ALIAS made by glob assignment is not honoured: after `*palatable2:: = *{"aliased::X::"}`, a sub compiled as `sub palatable2::sub {...}` lives in (and reports) PALATABLE2, where perl compiles it into the ALIASED stash.
PROBE scratch/s523b/p1/stash.pl (perl 5.40.3 / base 6cf75804 / tree):
  { no strict 'refs'; *palatable2:: = *{"aliased::X::"}; ${"palatable2::foo"} = 1; ${"palatable2::"}{"sub"} = ${"palatable2::"}{"foo"}; }
  my $t = eval 'sub palatable2::sub { (caller(0))[3] } \&palatable2::sub';
  $t->()                                  perl aliased::X::foo   PCL PALATABLE2::sub
  B::svref_2object($t)->GV STASH::NAME    perl aliased::X::foo   PCL PALATABLE2::sub
(Two facts: the stash alias `*a:: = *b::`, and the GV alias `$stash{sub} = $stash{foo}` that makes `sub palatable::sub` define the glob named foo.)  The upper case is #3671.
ROWS: Scalar-List-Utils t/exotic_names.t -- 388 rows (194 "stash name for natively compiled sub" + 194 "caller() in natively compiled sub", the ordinals that are NOT legal identifier characters; the 33 legal ones compile directly and pass).  Layer: the runtime's stash view (s522b's `p-stash` / stash-assign area) -- measure there first.
subject: A stash ALIAS (*a:: = *{"b::"}) plus a GV alias in it is not honoured: sub a::sub compiles into A, not the aliased stash -- SLU exotic_names.t 388 natively-compiled rows
